pattern.description: The UI cards (evaluation criteria, data collection, summary) drift up and dissolve. A centred two-line statement blurs in from soft grey to crisp black, with the key figure '32 languages.' in a warm gradient. Out-of-focus foreign-language words for 32 ('otuz iki') fade in at the lower right as depth texture.
pattern.why_premium: Blur-to-sharp focus pulls the eye from busy UI to a single claim without a cut. The gradient on the number marks the payoff, and the defocused translated words make 'multilingual' visible while adding depth layering instead of clutter.

build_hint.gsap: tl.to('.cards', {y: -200, opacity: 0, filter: 'blur(8px)', duration: 0.5, ease: 'power2.in'}); tl.fromTo('.line1', {opacity: 0, filter: 'blur(12px)', color: '#999'}, {opacity: 1, filter: 'blur(0px)', color: '#000', duration: 0.45, ease: 'power2.out'}, '-=0.2'); tl.fromTo('.line2', {opacity: 0, filter: 'blur(12px)'}, {opacity: 1, filter: 'blur(0px)', duration: 0.45, ease: 'power2.out'}, '<0.1'); tl.fromTo('.ghostWord', {opacity: 0}, {opacity: 0.35, duration: 0.5, stagger: 0.1}, '<').
build_hint.remotion: The cards use translateY interpolate(frame, [0, 15], [0, -200], {easing: Easing.in(Easing.quad)}) with opacity and blur. For line i: const p = spring({frame: frame - 9 - i*3, fps, config: {damping: 200}}); opacity = p, filter = `blur(${(1-p)*12}px)`. The ghost words fade in to 0.35 opacity, with blur kept at about 6px.

notes: camera.move is tilt_down (the cards drift up), but the main effect is the blur crossfade to the type card, so blur_crossfade is chosen over kinetic_word_reveal. The 'otuz iki' words are probably the first of a cycling multilingual ghost-word background (see the next events).
